x: Dave Baulch, again selected to run up Dale Hill, joined in the spirit of the chase and soon moved up to third place and was gaining fast on Woodford, who had by this time run all their best men and were beginning to flag badly.

Only Baulch and Gebbett ran true to form and finished in positions which deserve any special mention. Baulch especially was in fine fettle to finish 11th behind such names as Firth, Caulder, Barrett, Towl, Maynard, Clark and Driver, all of whom are in international class in one sphere or another.
Eric Gebbett was, as usual, quickly in the lead and he, together with Charlie Walker and Dave Baulch, took the field along at a very brisk pace.

No sooner had the second lap commenced than Pat decided to increase the tempo, only Dave Baulch attempting to go with him. However,on leaving the Common for Copse Hill Pat was way ahead and increasing his lead with every stride; the role of pack leader being taken over by Eric Gebbett.

Good times were recorded by Baulch, Bhatia, Davies and Newell. These two races,followed by our own 5¾ miles road race and 3 miles yacht handicap, preceded the London to Brighton Relay for Southern clubs on October 11th and we had every reason to think we were set for a place - in actual fact we had…

We need some new blood so before April let us see some form from such people as Miller, Thresher, Linstead, Johnston, Stearman, and a return to the team by Hallowell, Davies and Baulch (not new blood but almost indispensable).
…ing behind Linstead, Dabbs, Gebbett & Co. as they did the "seven hills"; sometimes on the "Warren 9" with Bird, Walker, Baulch & Co.…
Laurie O'Hara and Charlie Dabbs are close behind with 7 and it is interesting to note that the 'old school' of Walker, Dabbs, Newell and Baulch are jointly responsible for 26% of the list.

Thomas and Baulch also ducked well under 45 seconds in this classiest ever British one-lap race. John Regis had to dig deep and use every ounce of his strength to stay a millimetre or two ahead of Christie to take the 200m - both were given the same time to the hundredth.
